articles.title: Are We Legacy Computing Yet?
articles.summary: The Unicode "Symbols for Legacy Computing" (U+1FB00-U+1FBFF) and its supplement block (U+1CC00-U+1CEBF) contain graphical characters that were used on 70s, 80s, and 90s computers to display semi-graphical elements, such as pictures and games. These characters can be used to draw filled shapes, create graphical symbols, and enhance terminal UIs. The Unicode standard provides a way for terminals to draw these characters, but few fonts contain the necessary paths, so many terminals implement custom drawing routines. This allows for more precise control over graphical elements, even on devices with limited font support.

articles.title: RangeFrom, Part 2..: What I think is wrong about the design
articles.summary: The RangeFrom iterator is not designed to yield values beyond the largest value in the range, which can lead to unexpected behavior when overflow-checks are turned off. This is because the internal counter is incremented before the value is yielded, causing the iterator to overflow before the final value is reached. This can result in the iterator producing incorrect results, such as printing a value before it is actually yielded.

articles.title: Cancelation Terminology
articles.summary: A short note explaining the difference between synchronous cancelation, asynchronous cancelation, and graceful shutdown. Synchronous cancelation is an implicit control flow structure that unwinds the stack and involves error handling, typically breaking out of loops and invoking cleanup actions. Asynchronous cancelation is a communication protocol between two parties, such as a CPU thread pool or io_uring, where one party requests cancelation and waits for the other party to acknowledge it before proceeding. This phenomenon is relatively low-level and often required in concurrent programming, affecting the way developers write software.
